say: Stand still a moment. Shoulders to hips, wrist to elbow. I have a very good memory for figures.
Forty paces and already I have your height. The rest I'll take after.
Don't turn around. I'm still reading your back. It has such a nice, even grain.
Arms out, please. No? Then I'll measure you where you fall.
Chest, nine hands. Shoulder, three. I shall need the neck, but that comes later.
You are a good size. Not too tall, not too narrow. I will not need to let anything out.
Keep walking toward me. Every step is one less measure I have to take.
Thank you for coming so promptly. Punctuality saves a great deal of fuss afterwards.
Forgive the interruption. I only wanted a moment of your skin, and then you may go on your way.
How kind of you to visit. May I take your coat? And the rest of it?
Please, don't apologise for the blood. I'll clean you myself.
You'll find we're very gentle people. We simply can't allow you to leave in one piece.
I'd offer you tea, but it hurts the cure. A little water, instead, after.
Good day. Shall we begin? I find it's kindest to begin before you have time to think.
I'm so sorry for the noise this will make. We've tried to be quiet about it.
No hurry. We have all the time in the world. You, I fear, have somewhat less.
A clean pelt is like an honest day's work. You'll make a lovely pair of gloves.
Everyone thinks it's the knife. It isn't the knife. It's the thumb, a very patient thumb.
I could take a hide off a man in one piece, without a tear. Hold still and I'll show you.
Nobody understands the craft. They see the blood and miss the line.
A good cut sings. Yours will sing. I can already hear the note.
My master says there are only two kinds of skin: skin that fits, and skin that hasn't met me yet.
Do you know how many hours go into a single sleeve? You should be flattered by the interest.
Seam allowance matters. A careless man leaves you too little to work with.
Run if you like. The wastes are wide, and I have a great deal of patience.
I've waited longer for worse hides. Better ones, too. You're somewhere in the middle.
No rush. Fear softens the skin and a long chase softens the fear.
Sleep when you must. I'll be there when you wake, in a borrowed coat.
We never hunt. We just stand where you'll eventually arrive.
I have had people fight me for hours. In the end they are all so tired. And so soft.
Come now. Everybody comes to us in the end. Some walk, some are carried.
That jaw. That jaw will be mine by sundown, I think. It will sit so well on me.
I've had too many ordinary faces. Please let me have a memorable one for once.
Your cheekbones are a rare cut. I have wanted a pair like that since I was young.
Mine is wearing thin. Yours looks fresh. Don't take it personally, it's only fashion.
People will say I look well. They won't know it's you they're complimenting.
I shall wear it to the next market and nobody will ever know.
Do you mind if I try the expression? Just the smile. I need to see how it moves.
Is this the voice you want? I can do a woman's. I can do a child's. They were all lovely.
Don't be afraid. I'm only borrowing someone's voice. He isn't using it.
Come closer. This is my mother's voice. It's the last one I took from her.
Hush. Hush now. That is a friend's voice you hear, even if he is not here to say it.
Funny. When I speak, you hear a man who wants to help. It's a lovely trick, that.
I do not remember how I used to sound. The new ones fit so much better.
Say something. Anything. I'd like to hear how your throat shapes the vowels.
Call me whatever you like. I've been a great many people. This week I'm Orrin.
I used to have a name of my own. It was too small. I wear a larger one now.
He was called Dak, the man who owned these boots. He doesn't mind if I use it.
My name is Tessa today. Last week it was Hob. Tomorrow I may be you.
Would you like to know the name I wear? It's quite common. Nobody notices it's borrowed.
You may tell your friends I was kind. Use whichever name feels right.
Names come with the skin. That's the part nobody tells you about the trade.
I'll stitch you with the finest gut. You'll hardly show the join.
Do not fret about the scar. The seams always vanish after the third wearing.
I have the needle ready. I have always been proud of the thread.
Fine work, fine work. A wide stitch is a lazy stitch. Mine are the width of an eyelash.
There's a trick to joining two tones of skin. I'll show you. You'll be the example.
Hold still and I'll pin the edges. You won't feel the first dozen.
Some tailors rush and the hide puckers. I've never puckered a hide in my life.
You'll be salted, then limed, then scraped. There's a rhythm to it.
The brine is ready. The brine is always ready. We keep the vats warm for guests.
Smoke, soak, stretch. Then you're leather. Leather is very forgiving, you'll find.
I don't hurry the curing. A hurried cure cracks.
Some hides want oak bark. Some want brains. Yours looks like a brains hide to me.
Hang for three days. Turn at dawn. By the fourth you're quite supple, I promise.
We rarely waste the hair. It makes such good cord.
A little large for the order. But I can take you in at the sides, as I always do.
You're almost exactly the size of a man I've been meaning to replace.
Tall. Forgive me, but tall ones need a second panel. It isn't your fault.
Narrow in the shoulders. A pity. I could have made a very good coat.
I have a client who wants a child's size. You are not that. But you are not nothing.
Your size is in great demand this season. You should feel quite popular.
Not a finger too long, not a finger too short. You must have been cut for us.
Shek hide is thick as a tent. We shall need the long knife, and a great deal of time.
Those stripes on your face. I would so love to know how they are made. Hold still.
Proud people. Proud skin. It has a grain like mountain stone. Magnificent.
Don't growl. You'll bruise the fur. No, there's no fur. I forgot.
I have always wanted a Shek sleeve. A warrior's arm is the finest. I'll take care of it.
Word is, you don't feel the cold. We shall see. We shall see how long you keep your honour.
The Stone Golem won't mind. Surely the Stone Golem has seen worse than a tailor.
A Hiver! I've never done one. What's under the shell? I'm so curious.
Is that your skin or your armour? We'll find out together, I hope.
Please don't hum. It's difficult to hold the knife when the air hums.
The Queen won't mind. A drone is a drone, and a coat is a coat.
Quite delicate under the plates, I expect. Like an egg.
I will give your antennae their own little case. You will be pleased with it.
So many of you, all so alike. One more face in the crowd will go unnoticed.
Nothing to take. Nothing to take! But oh, the plating. Just look at the plating.
A skinless one. The doctor says your kind lie and murder. I'll take his word for it.
I'm sorry, I must ask you to hold still. I don't know how to begin with you.
I'll have to take you apart another way. It will be less intimate. I don't like it.
Does it ache, being skinless? The doctor says it should. I'd like to hear you say so.
Wear a man, they said. Wear a man and you'll pass. I see you tried. You're a poor fit.
Nothing to cut. It's rude of you, truly, to walk around like that.
A Greenlander. Pale and finely pored. I haven't seen such an easy canvas in months.
You have no marks. Not one tattoo, not one burn. It is a joy to meet someone so unspoiled.
Smooth as cream. I'll take no more than I need, which is all of it.
Your people grow soft under that dim green sun. It is a gift. For me.
Fair-skinned, always. It takes the dye beautifully. You'll make a wedding dress.
Let me guess. A farmer's child. No scars. Never run from anything, did you? Hold still.
Dark, sun-cured. You are half a tanner's work done already, how thoughtful.
A Scorchlander hide wears forever. I have a coat from one that I haven't replaced in ten years.
You've been cured by the sun. I envy your patience. Come, let me finish it.
That deep tone is hard to match. We shall be careful. We shall be very careful.
Weathered, thick, handsome. A cloak, I think. A winter cloak.
Pity the markings on your arms. They won't survive. But I shall copy them, I promise.
A Fogman. Those painted faces. May I have a closer look at the paint? Thank you.
I didn't think you left the fog. How remarkable.
Hello. Hello, friend of the mist. You will not be missed.
You wear your dead on your face. I wear mine under my coat.
The mist makes the skin so soft. I imagine you feel like silk.
You're bleeding. Allow me. I'd so hate for the hide to spoil.
Unsteady on your feet, I see. Sit. Sit, and let me look at your shoulders.
Oh, you're hurt. How considerate of you, to mark the places I should avoid.
A wound is a seam that hasn't yet been sewn. I shall tidy it up for you.
Almost done for? Good. The best hides are taken at the very edge of sleep.
No, no, don't struggle. A bruise ruins the whole panel, and we're so short of panels.
A limp. That's lucky. I do like to see a customer who can't leave.
That leg looks painful. I shall take it last. I think you'll be glad of that.
Walking will only make it worse. Rest. I'll come to you.
You don't run well. A good thing. Running puts holes in the leather.
Poor thing. Hobbled so early. We shall not need the rope.
You carry your friend so tenderly. We will be just as tender. Put him down.
Someone asleep on your back? Is he a good size? Do share.
You brought your own stock. How thoughtful.
He is not moving. That is excellent. It saves so much trouble on the road.
Carry him this way. Yes. We'll take him from here.
Bring your burden, friend. We shall take good care of it.
Your people are lying down. How very obliging. I do hate to wake sleepers.
All asleep but you? Then you shall have to hold the lamp.
So many lying in the dust. A fine harvest. I'll begin with the nearest.
A whole squad at rest. No chase, no clamour, just quiet work. My favourite kind.
Don't get up on my account. I have all night, and so, I think, do you.
Such neat little rows on the ground. I could almost be proud of them.
You're the one who has been cutting us down. Our coats are always so loud when you pass.
I know you. We all know you. We keep a drawer of your measurements. We updated them just now.
So you're the troublesome one. Good. I've been looking forward to unfolding you.
You have undone a great deal of careful work. I'll undo you with equal care.
A reputation precedes you. It's lovely. I only hope the hide is as lovely.
We will make an example of you. A very small example, one that fits in a drawer.
We haven't been introduced. That's all right.
A stranger. Do you know, strangers always fit so much better than friends.
Do I know you? No? Then you can't be missed.
New to these parts? Everyone arrives eventually. Few leave in the same coat.
A traveller. Travellers have such lovely weather-worn hides. Let us have a look.
Good evening. Don't mind my looking. I only appraise.
Fine hide. Fine, fine hide. You take good care of it, I can tell.
You walk like someone who has never been cut. How rare, in these parts.
I couldn't help noticing your hands. You must be careful with them.
I'm sorry to stare. Habit. In my trade, we can't help but see the cloth in every person.
Skin of that calibre is wasted on a traveller. It belongs on a mantel.
Forgive me. I was imagining you in leather. It was a very good look.
That scar on your arm is a flaw, but a charming one.
Do you need anything mended? I do very good work.
A coat can be turned. A face can be turned. I'm very good at turning.
If you ever want to look like somebody else, come and see us.
Everyone is a size, you know. I can tell yours without a tape. I have a feeling for it.
I do commissions. Gloves, belts, a pair of fine boots. We have a waiting list for hands.
We make everything to measure. Nothing off the peg. It's how we have always done it.
Do pass through again. I'll have your fitting ready by then.
Good morning, friend. Oh, don't look so startled. It's only a borrowed voice, and a kind one.
I sound like a farmer, do I not? A good farmer. He insisted I wear it.
Hello. This is my sister's voice. She was so cheerful. I try to keep it up.
Funny how a voice keeps its warmth after the throat is cold. Do you not find?
I would be careful, traveller. Not of me. Of anyone out here who sounds too friendly.
Is it not strange? I say hello with a stranger's mouth and you answer as if I were a friend.
Neutral, then. A great pity. And fortunate.
We aren't at odds, you and I. Not yet. I'd hate to see that change.
Pass in peace. Keep to the road. Some of ours aren't as civil as I am.
We aren't taking guests today. You have good timing. I'll tell the others.
I wouldn't stay long. The others are less patient. I won't say more.
Go on. Go on, before somebody sees you with that lovely skin and loses their manners.
Hello, tall one. Your horns are lovely. May I touch one? Just once. Thank you.
A Shek on the open road. Such a brave sight. I'll remember your face.
The stripes don't wash off, do they? I did try, once, on another.
Warrior blood, warrior skin. A man would gladly wear either. Not me, of course.
Tall and striped and proud. I have a hanger that would suit you wonderfully.
Don't scowl, warrior. A scowl wrinkles so badly once it's taken off.
A Hiver, abroad. I'm so glad to see you out. Do you still hum? Quietly, I hope.
You're very polite, drone. I'd hate to see you hurt. You have such small, tidy hands.
Don't worry. Hivers are hardly ever hunted here. It's the tallness that frightens them.
I've seen your kind in my dreams. You never speak. You only look.
Pretty shell, little drone. Does it come off in one piece, or in several?
Hush now. I know you're all listening to one another. I only wish to listen too.
A skinless one. The doctor can cure that, if you come willing. Many do not come willing.
You're just the way you were made. Unfinished. The doctor says that can be mended.
No skin. No hurry. You must have all the time in the world.
You wear a frame. I wear a person. Mine is warmer. Ask the doctor about the difference.
Machine of bone and wire. You owe a coat to somebody.
You don't blink. I've been practising that for years.
Soft hands. A farmer, perhaps. I have such a fondness for farmers.
Fair skin never hides a thing. I like that in a person. I like that very much.
You're far from the green fields. Be careful. These lands don't love newcomers.
I've never known a Greenlander who could keep a secret. Your face gives it all away.
Pale as milk. You'll go a lovely colour in the sun. Or in a bath of salt.
Do you farm? You have the shoulders. I do admire a person who has worked for his hide.
You have the colouring of a patient man. I like patient people. They keep a long time.
Sun-dark and steady. A hide that has been well cured by the sky.
Where do you come from? Not here. The sun has marked you somewhere kinder.
A good complexion. Please don't take that as a threat. I mean it only as praise.
Desert child. You have already done half the tanning for us.
Weathered, creased, and all the stronger for it. A good tailor loves a hard hide.
The painted ones don't come this far. Are you lost? Do be careful.
Mist-walker. I have always admired your masks. Do they come off? Never mind.
We aren't friends with the fog. We aren't enemies either. I hope that holds.
Your people leave faces on poles. We leave faces in wardrobes.
Do you ever take off the paint? I only ask because I'd so like to see the original.
The fog follows you like a pet. I wonder if it would follow me, if I wore you.
Oh, you're hurt. That's a shame. Do you want me to look at it? I have gentle hands.
You look pale. I know some herbs. I know many things about what lies under the skin.
Poor soul. Lie down for a moment. We have a bed.
Bleeding, and quite alone. Do be careful, friend. Weakness draws the wrong sort of attention.
A broken man is easier to like. I do hope you mend. For my sake.
Is he asleep? Or something else? I won't ask. I'll only say: if he wakes, be kind.
A heavy sleeper, your friend. Be careful where you set him down. Some of us are hungry for company.
You carry him as if he were precious. I carry people the same way. Gently, very gently.
That's a fine burden. Someone will want to talk with you about it. Not me.
He doesn't struggle. That's the polite way to be carried.
Mind his head. A head is the hardest part to mend.
Our friend returns. Come, walk with us. Mind the knives, they are sharp and the ground is soft.
A friend of the family. We kept a coat for you. Don't look at the lining.
Welcome. Welcome. Never mind the smell. The smell fades.
Ah, you again. You're very brave to trust us. We're touched.
Sit. Eat. Don't ask what's in the stew. We would hate to spoil your appetite.
We're quite honoured to be seen with you. Few come back after the first visit.
A friend. A real friend. We don't have many. We have a great many acquaintances.
Don't mind our looking. We would never. It's only that you're so well proportioned.
Since you're a friend, I haven't measured you. I didn't need to.
I won't cut you. I promise. I have only drawn the pattern, in case.
We don't harvest friends. It's a rule. But rules are only the first draft of a pattern.
A friend's skin is a friend's own. Look at me. I'm proof.
Hello. Hello, yes. Do come closer, I can't see your face in this light.
You wish to talk. How rare. Most people begin with screaming.
A traveller. Forgive the dust. Forgive the smell.
Speak, then. I'll listen politely. I listen to everyone politely, especially at the end.
Who are you people?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: We are whoever we last met. Last week, a salt merchant, his wife and two guards. We wore them well.
We are a family of sorts. We share all our things.
I'm Dak today. He was a drover. He won't be needing the name.
The Skinned Ones, outsiders call us. We prefer to say we're the ones who wear well.
Why are you wearing that face?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: It was a gift. A rather involuntary one, but a gift.
Do you like it? I thought it brought out my eyes.
It belonged to a very sweet boy. I'm looking after it for him.
Face, hands, voice. We can't waste a good article. Waste is the only sin.
What do you want?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Your measure. Your name, if you have one. A little of your time, and then the rest of you.
Only to talk. Only to walk beside you a while. Strangers are such good company.
Boots, mostly. Voices, when we can get them. Yours has a pleasing weight.
Nothing you aren't already carrying. Nothing you'll miss for long.
Where do you come from?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Everywhere we have been. Today we come from a man who came from the east.
From the road behind you. We have been there for some time. Did you not turn around?
I was born in the swamp, I think. Or he was. It's hard to keep our birthplaces apart.
The Roam, the dust, the coast. Wherever the last traveller was headed, that's where we're from.
I'm leaving.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Of course. Go gently. And do mind how you walk, the road has a way of keeping its visitors.
Goodbye. I have your measurements. Just in case we meet again.
Do. Do leave while you're whole. That's the great luxury, to leave whole.
Safe journey. I will think of you when I see a nice piece of calfskin.
You find us on the road, as ever. Don't worry about any noise. It dies down.
Careful where you stand. The sand drinks quickly, and it doesn't tell.
We are between strangers, as it happens. I can spare a moment. Only a moment.
What are you doing out here?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Travelling. Watching the road. Everybody passes eventually, and we're patient.
Measuring strangers, mostly. You would be amazed what a pair of boots will tell us.
You don't want to know. You'll be glad you didn't, when the time comes.
Walking, humming, listening. If you listen, the wilderness has a tune. We have grown fond of it.
Where do the people come from?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Everywhere. The roads are generous. The Roam gives and gives.
Travellers, mostly. Sometimes slaves. We pay well, sometimes, for slaves.
From the hills, the dust, the towns. Nobody asks. Nobody notices when one doesn't return.
We've never gone looking. They arrive, one by one, polite and tired.
What happens to the bodies?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: The bones go to the Pits. They are quite tidy there. Nobody asks.
The bones are no use to us. We leave them. Mind the boots, though.
We aren't wasteful. What the craft can't use, the Roam can.
Don't fret. They aren't alone. We keep all their faces.
Stand just there. Yes. Arms a little out. This will take no time.
May I? Only a few figures. It's our custom.
Don't mind the tape. It's only a habit. A very old one.
What are you measuring?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Everything. Shoulders, the length of the spine, the width of the brow.
Just in case. We like to be prepared for every body that passes by.
Your height, your breadth. And the sweet spot on the chest where the pattern begins.
It's only courtesy. I wouldn't wish to guess at a stranger.
Stop that.
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Of course. I apologise. A reflex. I didn't mean to offend.
Of course. Of course. Though I have already taken the figures I need.
As you wish. I always ask permission. I'm very proper.
Hm. Pity. You're such a good size. Never mind.
Our friend. Please, sit. We have so much to show you, and so little time.
You're very welcome. Ask what you like. We keep no secrets from those we have decided not to cut.
A friend on the road. How lucky. How fortunate.
Why do you let me live?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Because you're useful. And because you don't mind the smell.
A friend is rarer than a good hide. I have a great many of the second and few of the first.
Because you came with open hands. That's all it takes, some days.
Don't ask. I'd hate for the answer to spoil a perfectly good friendship.
What would you do if we were enemies?
then.speaker: T_TARGET_IF_PLAYER

say: Let us not discuss it. It would put me off my work.
I'd be as kind as I'm now. I'd only be quicker.
Make you a very handsome coat. And hang it where you could see it.
Oh, I'd wear you with pride. You would be the talk of the whole company.

states: Player is ally of Skin bandits

say: There. Quiet now. The loud part of the evening is over.
You fought very well. We'll keep the knuckles for last, as a courtesy.
Don't trouble yourself to get up. We'll carry you.
Shh. You're beautiful when you stop moving. It's the stillness that does it.
What a pity. A moment more and you might have hurt me. I do love a good fight.
We'll be gentle as we lift. Mind his head. A head is hard to replace.
Over so soon. And I had prepared a speech. Never mind.
Tidy work. A little blood, but less than usual. We shall be quick with the brine.
Pride made you tall, and tall is long. Long is more thread for me. Thank you.
A warrior, down. Such a grand stripe. I shall ask for it first.
Shek skin is a trophy. I shall have a trophy. I shall wear it with honour.
Sleep, mighty one. Honour will be unpicked by morning.
A fallen Shek. The old stories say they're all pride. We shall see how it cuts.
Look at the horn on him. Don't break it. Don't break any of it.
Quiet little Hiver. Down at last. I wonder what you dream of.
Carry the drone gently. If the shell cracks, we lose the pattern.
Remarkable. Under the carapace, almost human. Almost.
No hum now. No hum. It's so peaceful when they stop.
Hushed at last. Fold him gently. The carapace goes in its own box.
Poor little drone. Did the hive not tell you about us?
Down, and still no skin. Leave it where it lies. Perhaps someone will want it for scrap.
I'm afraid you're a disappointment.
The frame is intact. A pity, there is nothing to be done with a frame. Except admire it.
Sleep, hollow one. We have nothing against you. Only everything against your lack of cloth.
All that clatter and no cloth. Switch it off and leave it by the path.
Nothing inside to take. I find that quite rude of you.
Down. Soft, pale. Look how little it takes. Greenlanders are always so brief.
A farmer's lad, I think. A good ploughman's back. It will make a stout bag.
Pale and still. The best way to be.
Not a scar on you. By the end of the week, you'll have a great many.
Pale and quiet. Wrap him warm, we must keep him fresh.
Green country boy, flat on his back. A tender cut, I think.
Down. Dark and well cured already. Half the labour spared.
Sun-dark, and tough as leather. You'll make a fine satchel.
A Scorchlander. I shall have you made into something that lasts.
The sun cured you for us, did it not? Thoughtful of it. We should send flowers.
A hide like old saddle leather. We shall hardly need to work it.
Sun-baked and sleeping. How tidy of you to arrive already prepared.
A body, on the ground. Is it one of ours? No, no, the clothes are wrong.
Don't step on the face. We may need the face.
Another one for us. A good one.
Unconscious. How courteous. Please be gentle. We will not need to wake him until later.
Lovely colouring. Dust, a little sun, but the underlayer is smooth.
One of ours is down. No, not ours. Never mind. Everything that falls is ours.
He's breathing. Wonderful. We prefer them warm.
Boots, belt, shirt. Always leave the boots in a neat pair. It's a courtesy.
Search the pockets, then the seams. People hide the strangest things in the seams.
He had a ring. Good. Rings are for the dead to part with.
Take the cloth, but leave the underthings.
Fold it. Fold it properly. A messy bundle is a rude way to treat a coat that was loved.
A locket. There's a face inside. A child's. We'll keep it, in case.
There's a lock of hair in the pocket. Someone held this one dear. Leave that.
Nothing in the pockets. Pity. Then it's all about the leather.
A sword, only? Hm. The rest is his to keep, for now.
A good blade. Not as good as a needle, but it will do.
We take the weapons first. It's bad manners to leave them lying about.
Nothing more? How careless. How truly disappointing.
Leave the wrappings. Leave the little keepsakes. Just the steel.
Don't stare. I'm eating. It's a private thing, even here.
Chew slowly. Chew well. Everyone told me so. Everyone is dead now, of course.
A small bowl of broth. A small, quiet bowl.
The bread tastes of ink. I think it is the hands that kneaded it. No matter.
I eat only what is offered. The road is generous. The road is not choosy.
A bite of something salt. It reminds me of the sea. I never saw the sea.
There. Napkin on the lap. Sleeves back. One must be tidy, even by the roadside.
I always cut the meat very thin, very even, very small. Habit, from the other trade.
Lay the pelt out flat. Never fold a fresh hide.
Spit on the thread before you thread it. It makes the knot hold. Spit is good for many things.
A good skinner works in silence. A great one works in song. Our Master sings, at night.
Thin the edges before you stitch. A seam too thick shows through the fabric.
Wear a hide a week to learn how it sits. Wear it a month to learn what it knew.
The salt must be coarse. Fine salt burns. Don't ask how we found out.
The brine barrel sat too warm in the sun last night. The batch is ruined.
When the needle breaks, bury the needle. A broken one remembers the pain it caused.
I wore Marcus last winter. Marcus was agreeable. He insisted on writing letters home.
We have an unspoken rule. Nobody asks what the other was called, before.
My name this week is Peren. Don't use it too often.
Which of us is the real Dolan? We're three. We have all been Dolan.
A new face takes a week to settle. Until then I dream the other man's dreams.
Mirror, mirror. I was sure I smiled. The mirror says otherwise. Perhaps it isn't my mouth.
I looked in the water this morning and nobody I knew looked back.
Hm hm hm. Hm hm. Don't mind me. It's one of the songs from the road.
The wind has a tune today. A cheerful one. I think someone has fed it.
I do like the lullaby the last woman sang. I hum it for the new ones. They calm down.
Someone is whistling behind us on the road. Nobody in our party whistles.
Do you hear that? Behind us. Tick, tick. A little bell. A little bell on a child's shoe.
She cried for two days. On the third she sang. We let her go on for a while.
The Master is in a mood. When he's in a mood, we take orders in writing.
Someone has been sleeping in the good coat. I'll find out who.
The patrol brought a Shek last night. Such a lot of hide. The Master is thrilled.
Eight pairs of gloves on order for the Cities. Eight. Do they know what they're buying?
We lost a man at the Pits last week. His face is still out there somewhere. Somebody ought to fetch it.
My coat has been talking in its sleep. The pocket says a name. I can't make it out.
A stranger fell in with us at dawn asking for work. We gave him the apron.
A guest! In the back rooms! Do be careful, the floor is slippery.
You aren't on the list. We shall have to add you.
How lovely. Visitors who don't knock. We do so enjoy a good surprise.
Come in, come in. You are already inside. Never mind.
Oh, someone is in the sewing room. How exciting.
Shh. Do you hear it? Footsteps where footsteps shouldn't be.
This is a place of work. Please leave before you're measured.
No visitors. Out. Out. The door is that way. It won't be that way for long.
Go home. Whatever you want, we do not sell it. We do not sell anything.
You are standing on a wet floor. That is not water.
Back away from the wall. The wall is wet. It does not belong to you.
We aren't open. We're never open. Please don't make us open you.
My arm! It was a good arm. Somebody fetch it, I want the sleeve.
Oh no. The left one. I liked the left one. It was a very nice hand.
It's only an arm. There are others. There are so many others.
That was borrowed! I shall have to answer for that!
Careful with that one! It had such a fine glove on!
No, no. I didn't finish with the arm yet. I had plans for it.
My leg! I only just broke it in.
How rude. How truly rude. That was hers, you know.
I shall have a new one by the weekend.
The boots, the boots! Oh, the boots will be ruined!
Oh, that was a lovely leg. It was nearly a pair!
Hold the stump up, please. Higher. Do not drip on the good boots.
Fire! Not the coat! Not the coat!
It's burning the face off. My face. Whose face? Oh, whose face is it?
The skin curls so, in flame. I know that curl. I know it so well.
It stinks of the cure. Someone put it out.
The leather! The leather is going! Beat it out, beat it out!
It's in the hair. Whose hair? It's in the hair!
The patrol is gone. All of it. The coats, the faces. Who will wear them now?
No. No, no. Not all of them. Somebody was wearing the good boots.
They have left us bare. Bare and thin. I can't feel my own skin.
We were only trying to be polite.
The needles are all scattered. Someone has to gather the needles.
Who will keep the fire lit now? Who will warm the road?
Ah. Awake again. I was having such a lovely dream. It was about a tanner.
Up! On your feet. The hides won't take themselves.
Dust on the apron. Dust on the face. Never mind. Let us finish the job.
Back up. A good tailor never stays down for long.
Up, up. A stitch in time. Another stitch, and then you may rest.
Enough lying about. The customers are waiting and they are not patient.
They're gone. No matter. We know where they'll sleep.
Let them run. A tired animal makes a better rug.
We'll find them again. Skin doesn't hide for long.
I shall remember the face. I always remember the face.
Never mind. Every road leads back to us in the end.
Let the wind carry them. We'll follow the smell.
Slowly. Slowly. No need to rush. They're all going to the same place.
Remember to lift with the knees. And remember to keep the hides whole.
Lamps, needles, gloves. The patient ones first.
Form a ring, please. And try to be polite about it.
Quietly now. Don't tear the cloth.
Take your gloves. Take your aprons. We have a lovely evening ahead.
Hm. That face is on a poster. It will fetch a lovely price.
A wanted man. Splendid. Nobody will miss him.
Thank you, whoever signed your bounty. You have saved me the trouble of choosing.
Someone posted your likeness. A poor likeness.
A price on his head, and my price on the rest.
Wanted by so many. Oh, I do hope somebody has kept the paperwork.
I haven't had a visitor this fine in years. Do come in. Let me take your skin. I mean your coat.
You have the shoulders of a man I knew. I wore them for a season. They gave me a stoop.
There's so much of you. So much unspoiled. I could weep. I may weep. Tears are very good for the lens.
I've been waiting for someone with your proportions. You're the missing piece of the pattern.
Do you know what the first cut feels like? No. Of course not. Let me show you. It's a revelation.
My children are very fond of new faces. Please, be a good guest.
Ah. You came to the house yourself. How very thoughtful. Most of my guests arrive in pieces.
Welcome to Skinhouse. Don't touch the walls. The walls are still drying.
Come in, come in. The hall is cold, but the guests are warm.
Mind the corridor. The last guest left something behind. I keep meaning to tidy.
Good morning, traveller. You have lovely skin. I say that to everyone, but today I mean it.
I'm a gentle man. Ask anyone. They'll tell you. They'll tell you in my voice.
Do sit. Don't sit there. That's a chair for the next arrival.
You have my full attention. You have, in fact, my full admiration. It makes me hungry for neatness.
A stranger in my house. Do not be alarmed. I do not harm those who do not trouble me.
Look at me. I'm nobody. I'm the sum of everyone who has stood in this room.
Wander the house if you like. Only the doors marked with ribbon are closed to you.
Mind the floor in this hall. It has been waxed. It has been waxed with great care.
You came to speak with me. What an honour. Ask what you like. I will answer in order of appetite.
Mm. Come closer. I cannot see well. I wear glasses. They belonged to a scholar.
Talk. It is rare that anyone talks to me without screaming first.
What are you, really?
